newsitem.title: USA: Duff & Phelps rates Mexican yen bond as Double-B.
newsitem.headline: Duff & Phelps rates Mexican yen bond as Double-B.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Thursday it has assigned a Double-B rating to the 100 billion yen Samurai bond issue from Mexico.
The five-year bonds have a 3.1 percent coupon.
The rating is supported by Mexico's "fiscal discipline and monetary policies, which successfully abated inflation and interest rates in 1996," Duff & Phelps said in a statement.
Duff & Phelps said it believes the country's vulnerability to unexpected shocks has been considerably reduced.
The rating also reflects the lingering effects of the 1994 peso crisis and Mexico's low domestic savings.
"However, DCR recognizes progress in each of these areas," it said.
